title: VTI session refusal and step-up handoff preservation

subject.system: OpenVTC VTI vtc-client / session and HTTPS Trust Task consumers
subject.scope: typed refusal preservation, step-up binding and non-authorizing outcomes across transport

proposition: A VTC client must preserve the full trust-task-error refusal and stepUpHandoff context over session/TSP transports without granting authority to retry or resume an operation outside its original principal, purpose, context, duration or session.

lifecycle.reason: Exact source-controlled direct Registry intake, operator-mediated GitHub owner reread; not migrated monitored Toolkit case and no change to Toolkit publishers.

assessment.basis: Source-level upstream reported tests and live example are not independently executed RAHP consuming-path evidence; canonical assessment will preserve absent evidence as indeterminate.

sources.claim: Merged VTI client transport change and reported upstream regression/e2e tests; no independent RAHP consuming-path replay or assurance determination.

residuals.question: Are trust-task-error refusals and stepUpHandoff typed and non-authorizing across session/TSP, HTTPS and Parked, including wrong-purpose and target substitution?
Are replay, expired/stale handoff, session binding changes, ambiguous retries and unexpected step-up completion prevented from causing unauthorized execution?

reassessment.trigger: Source-pinned independent consuming-path negative tests, transport changes, new step-up semantics, or corrected upstream implementation after reviewed merge.
